# Trufl


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

After a nuclear accident you cannot sample every field, and you have to decide before you know enough. trufl helps you decide **which areas to sample next and how many samples to take in each**, then revise that decision as results arrive.

A round has five steps: **describe** each area, **rank** the areas, **allocate** the budget, **place** the samples and **measure**. Then the next round begins, knowing more.

trufl supports a decision and does not make one. It does not know where it is safe to send people, and it does not say whether land or food is safe. It is alpha software, [not validated for operational use](https://franckalbinet.github.io/trufl/explanation/limits.html).

## Why trufl

Emergency data rarely meet the assumptions of sampling theory, and the reasons to sample one place before another change as an emergency develops. trufl uses criteria and weights that you choose and can inspect, so that each plan can be explained and challenged. [Where trufl comes from](https://franckalbinet.github.io/trufl/explanation/background.html) gives the reasoning and the research behind it.

## Install

With Python 3.10 or later:

`pip install trufl`

Version 0.2.1 and earlier compute the prior of an area too low. Until a later version is released, install from the source:

`pip install git+https://github.com/franckalbinet/trufl`

The tutorial has its own installation, because it needs the example map from the repository.

## Acknowledgements

trufl started within the IAEA Coordinated Research Project D15019, [“Monitoring and Predicting Radionuclide Uptake and Dynamics for Optimizing Remediation of Radioactive Contamination in Agriculture”](https://www.iaea.org/newscenter/news/new-crp-monitoring-and-predicting-radionuclide-uptake-and-dynamics-for-optimizing-remediation-of-radioactive-contamination-in-agriculture-crp-d15019), led by the [Joint FAO/IAEA Centre of Nuclear Techniques in Food and Agriculture](https://www.fao.org/agriculture/fao-iaea-nuclear-techniques/en). It is actively maintained.

It builds on the PhD research of Floris Abrams at [SCK CEN](https://www.sckcen.be) and [KU Leuven](https://www.kuleuven.be). Floris Abrams and Franck Albinet wrote the package. [Where trufl comes from](https://franckalbinet.github.io/trufl/explanation/background.html) describes the research and how trufl works with DSS4NAFA.
